Contents Foreign Exchange Impact on Revenue Changes in foreign exchange rates had an unfavorable impact on our revenue in the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. To calculate revenue on a constant currency basis, we translated revenue using the prior year's monthly exchange rates for our settlement or billing currencies other than the U.S. dollar. Using these constant rates, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, our total revenue and advertising revenue would have been $64.71 billion and $63.16 billion, which were $113 million and $96 million higher than actual total revenue and advertising revenue, respectively. Changes in foreign exchange rates had a favorable impact on our revenue in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Using prior year's monthly exchange rates, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our total revenue and advertising revenue would have been $179.39 billion and $175.11 billion, which were $2.32 billion and $2.34 billion lower than actual total revenue and advertising revenue, respectively.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the average price per ad increased by 14% and 13%, respectively, year-over-year, as compared with increases of 10% in both periods in 2025. The increases in average price per ad in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 were driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mostly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools. A favorable foreign currency exchange impact also contributed to the increase in the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Other factors are discussed in the section entitled "—Executive Overview of Third Quarter Results." In addition, the online commerce vertical was the largest contributor to the increase in advertising revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025.
